title: Language and daily life: French reach, commutes and household size
question: Which official language will I need day to day, and how do people get around?
dek: 2021 Census figures for each place's metropolitan area or agglomeration show where French is the working language, where both languages are common, and how commuting differs.

leadStat.label: Québec City: knows English and French

leadHeadline: French is nearly universal in 4 Quebec places (90–99%), but only 41–65% of residents also speak English

title: Climate: how cold, how snowy and how hot
question: What will the weather be like where I might live, especially in winter?
dek: 1991–2020 Environment and Climate Change Canada normals at one representative station per place, from the mild Pacific coast to the Arctic.
leadHeadline: January means span -26 °C (Iqaluit) to +4.6 °C (Victoria); only 3 places (Victoria, Vancouver, Abbotsford–Mission) average above freezing

title: Asking rents range from about $1,040 to $2,280 for a 1-bedroom, and advertised rents are usually above what the CMHC survey finds tenants pay
question: Where are rents lower, how have they changed, and how do advertised rents compare with what existing tenants pay?
dek: What a new lease costs on listing sites in 2026-Q2, how it moved in the past year and since 2019, and how it compares with CMHC's survey of rents actually charged.
leadHeadline: 1-bedroom asking rents run from $1,040 in Sherbrooke to $2,280 in Vancouver

title: With no income, a $15,000 buffer covers about 4 to 6 months for a single adult depending on the city
question: If I arrive with savings and no income yet, how many months could I cover housing and everyday costs in each place?
dek: A transparent scenario: sourced asking rent plus Market Basket Measure non-shelter costs, scaled to household size. Change the assumptions to match your situation.

leadStat.label: median months of runway, single adult, $15,000

leadHeadline: A single adult with $15,000 and no income lasts about 5.9 months in Sherbrooke but 4.0 in Vancouver

title: Read regional wages with their period and source method
question: What do employed workers earn in the economic regions around these places?
dek: Job Bank low, median and high wages, grouped by comparable period and methodology.
leadHeadline: Registered nurses: comparable regional medians range from $39.38 to $58.00 per hour

title: Job markets differ by several points between Canadian cities, and the year-on-year moves are mostly small
question: Which cities have tighter labour markets, and how are conditions changing?
dek: Labour Force Survey rates for comparable whole-CMA areas, with other places shown on their published geography.
leadHeadline: Unemployment ranges from 4.0% in Sherbrooke to 9.3% in Kelowna (three months to 2026-09)

title: Five years after admission, income differs by admission category (2018 cohort)
question: What have earlier immigrant cohorts earned, and how do their histories differ?
dek: Historical taxfiler medians, 2023 tax year, in 2023 constant dollars. These are not forecasts for a new arrival.
leadHeadline: Median employment income at year five: $70,300 for economic principal applicants and $26,400 for refugees

title: New permanent residents by intended destination in 2025, and historical provincial retention
question: Where do new permanent residents intend to settle, and who remains in their intended province?
dek: Admissions describe the destination at landing; retention describes tax residence years later. They are separate measures.
leadHeadline: Admissions per 1,000 residents range from 5.9 to 23.3 among comparable CMAs in 2025
